name: MatchData
description: What a successful match hands the guest, and how it is read.

scenarios.title: A match lists the whole match before its captures
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code converts a match to an Array
scenarios.then: the whole match comes first, then each capture

scenarios.title: A named capture is reachable by its name as a Symbol
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match by a capture name written as a Symbol
scenarios.then: it answers that capture

scenarios.title: The same name written as a String reaches it too
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match by a capture name written as a String
scenarios.then: it answers that capture

scenarios.title: A match knows where it started
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's beginning
scenarios.then: it answers the byte offset where the match starts

scenarios.title: A match knows where it ended
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's end
scenarios.then: it answers the byte offset just past the match

scenarios.title: The two are readable as one pair
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's offset
scenarios.then: it answers the beginning and the end together

scenarios.title: A match knows the text before it
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's preceding text
scenarios.then: it answers the substring before the match

scenarios.title: A match knows the text after it
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's following text
scenarios.then: it answers the substring after the match

scenarios.title: The captures alone are readable without the whole match
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's captures
scenarios.then: it answers each group and not the whole match

scenarios.title: Named captures map each name to what it caught
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's named captures
scenarios.then: each name maps to its captured substring

scenarios.title: A match lists the names it carries
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's names
scenarios.then: they come back in order

scenarios.title: Named captures can be keyed by Symbol on request
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's named captures asking for symbolized names
scenarios.then: the keys are Symbols

scenarios.title: A match's size counts itself as well as its groups
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's size
scenarios.then: it counts the whole match plus each group

scenarios.title: A match arises from matching and nowhere else
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code tries to construct a match directly
scenarios.then: a no-method error is raised

scenarios.title: Indexing with a start and a length answers that slice
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match with a start and a length
scenarios.then: it answers that slice of the group list

scenarios.title: Indexing with a range answers that slice
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match with a Range
scenarios.then: it answers that slice of the group list

scenarios.title: A negative index counts from the end of the list
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match with a negative index
scenarios.then: it answers the group that far from the end

scenarios.title: A name the pattern never declared is an error, not nothing
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code indexes a match by a capture name the pattern does not declare
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: A beginning past the group count is an error
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's beginning for an index past its group count
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: So is an end past the group count
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's end for an index past its group count
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: And an offset past it
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's offset for an index past its group count
scenarios.then: an index error is raised

scenarios.title: A group's beginning is reachable by the group's name
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads a match's beginning for a capture name
scenarios.then: it answers that group's byte offset

scenarios.title: A group that did not take part has no beginning
given: a Sandbox over the regexp-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code reads the beginning of a valid group that did not participate
scenarios.then: it answers nothing

text: A match is a snapshot the guest reads several ways — as a list, by number,
by name, and as offsets into the subject. Each reading is witnessed on its
own because they are separate accessors over one state, and one of them
drifting would not disturb the others.
The out-of-range readings are errors rather than absences, while a group
that was in range and simply did not participate answers nothing. Telling
those two apart is what lets guest code branch on an optional group without
A match cannot be constructed. It exists because a pattern matched, which is
what makes the offsets it carries mean anything about the subject it names.
